conventions.convention: Parity is modulo two. The total gauge-fixed transformation is Q=s+δ; its square is the declared symmetry H, and Q is called nilpotent only on a sector where H vanishes.

The gauge action is δ_gauge(u)A=−D_Au and δ_gauge(u)X=[u,X]. The lifted spacetime action is separated from the gauge-covariant Lie derivative; the source-ordered R bilinear and affine ghost transformation retain their displayed signs.

A finite regulator integrates the top exterior-degree component over its whole oriented finite-dimensional field manifold. Q-invariance means the exact integrated identity on the specified integrands, including absence of boundary flux.

The Ward identity concerns one fixed regulator and bundle sector, finite real parameters in a nonempty open interval, differentiability outside one common null set, measurable zero-extended derivatives, and compact-parameter integrable majorants. It asserts no continuum, saddle-limit, or regulator-removal theorem.
The toy integrals use dimensionless coordinates, Q=d, orientation dx∧dy, and the exterior-algebra exponential. The torus has both angular periods 2π; the cylinder has x∈[0,1] and y modulo 2π.
The cylinder cycle includes both boundary circles and imposes no condition cancelling their flux; with orientation dx∧dy its displayed Q-boundary integral is +2π.

load_bearing.statement: A gauge-fixed supersymmetry fluctuation datum specifies the field bundles, gauge fixing, Faddeev–Popov operator, ghosts, auxiliaries, odd transformation Q and its square H. At a Q-fixed configuration it defines the linearization D=(dQ), with D²=dH. A finite-dimensional regulator is separate additional integration and transformation data; no regulator existence, determinant evaluation, or continuum measure follows.

For one fixed sector of the adopted massless N=4 SU(2) round-S4 model, suppose a separately supplied finite-dimensional regulator realizes its declared total Q transformation and square. For smooth even Sρ,Oρ, smooth odd Vρ and a nonempty open parameter interval J, assume QρSρ=QρOρ=0, (Qρ²Vρ)Eρ,t=0, Iρ(Qρ(OρVρEρ,t))=0 without anomaly or boundary contribution, and the stated integrability, common-null-set differentiability, measurability and compact-parameter L1-majorant hypotheses. Then Zρ(t)=Iρ(OρEρ,t) is constant on J and Zρ′(t)=−Iρ(Oρ(QρVρ)Eρ,t)=−Iρ(Qρ(OρVρEρ,t))=0. This holds only at finite parameters for that fixed regulator and sector.

published_dependencies.used_for: The cited finite-dimensional deformation theorem applies this published result on a small open parameter interval inside a compact subinterval of J. Its uniform derivative majorant and common almost-everywhere differentiability hypotheses are retained.
The finite-dimensional deformation theorem uses the real difference-quotient definition componentwise for its complex-valued integral.
The finite-dimensional deformation theorem applies this published real-valued result separately to the real and imaginary parts after establishing continuity and zero derivative on J.

concerns.concern: The Definition introduces the concrete round-sphere formulas with “For the round-sphere model used in this page” but declares only def-qftx-susy-background-data and def-finite-dimensional-q-exact-localization-data as prerequisites. The first is generic and explicitly requires each model to supply its transformations and conventions; it does not define ε, ε̃, Γ̃_AB, β_v,P, φ, the affine ghost rule, or the completed sectorwise gauge fermion used here. Those concrete definitions are supplied by post-qftx-rigid-supersymmetric-background, which is neither linked nor declared in this definition's deps. The exact earlier model supplier should be identified and the formulation dependency recorded.

The configuration space is initially only “a specified subset” of a smooth-section space, but the next paragraphs use its tangent fluctuations and define D_Φ*=(dQ)_Φ*, asserting D_Φ*²=(dH)_Φ*. No differentiable structure on that subset, differentiability class for Q, or precise alternative formal linearization is required. Arbitrary contour and gauge constraints need not define a smooth configuration manifold. State the local smooth graded field-space/domain assumptions, or define linearization directly for the declared smooth differential transformations, so that these derivatives and their composition have a specified meaning.

seams_checked.note: The Ward theorem faithfully treats the round-S4 postulate as adopted physical data and preserves its formal measure and unconstructed regulator qualifications. The fluctuation definition's missing explicit model prerequisite is recorded separately in concerns. The source qualification is supported by Pestun, p. 4: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0712.2824.

The mathematical supplier was opened. Its graded algebra, integrated Q-invariance, Q²V condition, common-null-set differentiability, measurable derivatives and compact-parameter majorants are preserved. No fixed-locus formula or infinite-dimensional conclusion is imported.

The torus example checks the supplier's hypotheses and computes Z=4π²λ directly. The cylinder computes Z=−2πt and the obstructing Q-boundary integral +2π, explicitly excluding itself from the invariant theorem.

The S3 prerequisite is contextual: its ABJM postulate does not invoke the massless SU(2) S4 Ward theorem as a theorem about ABJM. Its field-space measure, deformation invariance and localization calculation remain explicitly adopted formal inputs.

The S4 consumer distinguishes its massive N=2* U(2) model from the massless N=4 SU(2) model. Its separate regulated Ward theorem applies the mathematical finite-dimensional supplier with matching explicit hypotheses, and does not infer a regulator, saddle limit, pole identification or continuum formula from this batch's theorem.
